title: The self made of bliss
hookLine: the Taittiriya goes two layers deeper and finds the Hindu teaching that the self, at its center, is joy
carry: at the center of you is ananda, joy
tomorrow: "words and mind turn back from it"
last: INSIDE THE BODY, BREATH; INSIDE BREATH, MIND.

lines: THE MUSK IS IN THE DEER.
TWO MORE LAYERS, TO THE CENTER.
cards: There's an old picture the poet-saint Kabir sang about. A musk deer catches a scent so sweet it can't rest. It runs the whole forest, nosing under every bush, looking for where that smell is coming from.
It never finds it, because the musk is in its own body. Kabir's point: the one we search for is already inside. The Taittiriya Upanishad makes the same search the slow way.
Peel back a person: food, then breath, then mind. And it keeps going, two more layers, to the very center. What it finds there isn't fear.

teach.h: INSIDE MIND, A SELF MADE OF UNDERSTANDING.
teach.b: Section four. Inside the self made of mind, the text says, is a self made of understanding. Vijnanamaya.
One way to hear the difference: mind, yesterday, was the part that learns and repeats; understanding sees what the learning is for, and acts on it. The text draws it, like the others, as a bird.

teach.h: ITS HEAD IS FAITH; ITS WINGS, ORDER AND TRUTH.
teach.b: Faith, shraddha, is its head. Rita, the right order of things, is one wing. Satya, truth, is the other.
Yoga is its body. Mahas, greatness, is its tail. Faith at the head is worth a second look: here understanding doesn't start from doubt.
It starts from trust, and grows into truth. Then section five. Inside understanding is a self made of bliss.
Anandamaya. Its head is priya, what is dear. One wing is moda, delight.
The other is pramoda, great delight. Its body is ananda, bliss itself. And its tail, the ground it rests on, is Brahman.
Vedanta teachers argue over the details.

teach.h: INSIDE THAT, A SELF MADE OF BLISS.
teach.b: Shankara read the bliss-self as one last layer, with Brahman beneath it; other teachers held that the bliss-self is Brahman itself.
But both readings point the same way, and this is the big Hindu teaching underneath: at your core you are not a scared animal or an empty hole.

teach.h: SAT, CHIT, ANANDA: BEING, AWARENESS, JOY.
teach.b: Later teachers put it in three words, sat, chit, ananda: being, awareness, joy, and many hear this chapter in them.
Joy, on this teaching, isn't a prize out in the forest. It's the musk. It's what you are, under the layers.

how: In Vedanta study, students learn the five layers in order, food to bliss, and teachers often use them as a guided meditation that moves attention inward from the body to the quiet center.

o: the mind that learns and repeats the Veda
vijnana, the fourth self: faith at its head
the bliss at the very center of a person

games.q: the last two layers — tap the pairs.

s: in the Taittiriya, the innermost self is made of bliss
anandamaya: inside understanding, a self made of joy, resting on Brahman.
all Vedanta teachers agree the bliss-self is Brahman itself
Shankara read it as one more layer, with Brahman beneath; others read it as Brahman.
later Vedanta teachers call the self sat-chit-ananda: being, awareness, joy
a later phrase, not this text's words, but many teachers hear this chapter in it.

games.q: you peel back the layers of a person: food, breath, mind, understanding. what does the Taittiriya say is at the center?
games.why: anandamaya: a self made of bliss, with what is dear as its head and Brahman as its foundation.

practice: Feel the body, then the breath, then the chatter of the mind, and let the chatter run a little farther off, like a radio in another room.

Notice whatever is noticing all of that, and see if there's anything there, even faintly, like ease: the relief of sitting down, the warmth of your own hands. If something like that shows up, rest in it; if it doesn't, rest anyway.

wordCard.voice: Understanding. Vijnana, the fourth layer in the Taittiriya: faith at its head, order and truth for wings, and inside it, the self made of bliss.

orig.note: Sanskrit ānandamaya: ānanda, bliss, + maya, made of. the fifth and innermost self in Taittiriya 2.5.

carryVoice: Your line: at the center of you is ananda, joy. The musk was never out in the forest. Until tomorrow.
